focus.rationale: Best non-AI agricultural cash-flow diversification lead in the present shortlist. H1 2026 cash generation is credible, though net income includes a one-off litigation gain and the nitrogen cycle can reverse.
focus.mustProve: Does $118–119 hold, then a close above $122–123 arrive with sustainable nitrogen margins, free cash flow and farmer affordability?
focus.risk: Gas input costs, supply normalisation, weaker fertiliser volumes and Blue Point investment may reduce apparent earnings quality.

focus.rationale: Existing nuclear-defence operating cash flow is clearer than the economics of pre-revenue reactor developers. Q2 raised adjusted earnings and FCF guidance; valuation is still demanding.
focus.mustProve: Can 2026 government/commercial nuclear orders fund backlog conversion and FCF while the shares base near $131–135 then reclaim $140 and $143–144?
focus.risk: Government programme shifts, PCG integration, growth capex and a valuation near 28.6× full-year adjusted EPS guidance midpoint.

focus.rationale: Electrical Americas orders, equipment backlog and Q2 free cash flow demonstrate actual supplier demand. The market price still embeds substantial future execution.
focus.mustProve: Will funded electrical orders translate into earnings and cash while $386 holds and $403–405 is reclaimed?
focus.risk: Customer financing delays, margins failing to follow orders, and valuation near 29× adjusted FY2026 EPS guidance midpoint.

focus.rationale: Marketplace improvement is promising, but the proposed $1.49bn Atome 60% purchase changes the investment into a much larger consumer-credit and capital-allocation question. Closing is expected by Q3 2027, not completed.
focus.mustProve: Can loan impairments, lending funding and the performance-linked remaining 40% purchase coexist with sustainable free cash flow? Hold $2.85–2.90, then regain $3.03/$3.15 before an entry discussion.
focus.risk: Credit losses, funding costs, large cash acquisition commitment and weaker-than-expected consumer-credit returns.

focus.rationale: Micron remains a real, profitable AI-memory supplier, but chip-sector price recovery does not prove durable HBM cash margins or customer orders against future capacity competition.
focus.mustProve: Verify paid HBM demand and inventory/pricing before treating a $931 then $950 reclaim as leadership repair; 19 Oct close was $904.90.
focus.risk: Reversal in memory pricing, customer spending delays, HBM margin disappointment and China memory supply.

focus.rationale: Vertiv helps keep data centres powered and cool. More powerful AI servers need more electricity and better cooling.
focus.mustProve: Are cooling orders linked to financed data centres converting to delivered revenue, cash and sustainable margins?
focus.risk: If AI projects are delayed, growth could slow while expectations remain high.

focus.rationale: Xylem supplies water systems for industry, cities and other essential users. New factories and data centres add to that demand.
focus.mustProve: Will strong customer orders translate into real sales and cash?
focus.risk: A growing order book is not the same thing as money in the bank.

focus.rationale: GE HealthCare makes medical imaging systems and is expanding in diagnostic technology. AI may help doctors use those tools more effectively.
focus.mustProve: Can new products and acquisitions add enough profits to justify their costs?
focus.risk: Debt, integration costs and slower hospital spending could limit returns.
